description: ASCII merger tree format produced by Rockstar (halo finder) and Consistent Trees (tree builder). Each tree_*.dat file contains a flat list of halos across all trees in that file shard. Trees are delimited by '#tree <Tree_root_ID>' comment lines. Halos within each tree are ordered depth-first. Pointer fields are reconstructed from global halo IDs and depth-first index fields.
references: Behroozi et al. (2013), ApJ 762, 109 — Consistent Trees https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/762/2/109
Behroozi et al. (2012), ApJ 756, 2 — Rockstar https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/756/1/2

Descendant.target_units: integer index within Tree<X> halo array
Descendant.notes: desc_id == -1 indicates no descendant (root halo). Mapped to tree-local flat index via id_to_local_index dict built per tree.

FirstProgenitor.target_units: integer index within Tree<X> halo array
FirstProgenitor.notes: In depth-first ordering, halo at local_index i has its first progenitor at local_index i+1 if that halo's desc_id equals this halo's id; otherwise -1.

NextProgenitor.target_units: integer index within Tree<X> halo array
NextProgenitor.notes: Converted to tree-local index by subtracting the tree's base Depth_first_ID and looking up via local dfi_to_index map. -1 when Next_coprogenitor_depthfirst_ID == -1.

FirstHaloInFOFGroup.target_units: integer index within Tree<X> halo array
FirstHaloInFOFGroup.notes: upid is the ID of the most massive host halo (top-level FOF central). If upid == -1 the halo is itself a central: self-pointer. Otherwise map upid to tree-local index at the same snap_num.

NextHaloInFOFGroup.target_units: integer index within Tree<X> halo array
NextHaloInFOFGroup.notes: Built by grouping halos at each snapshot by their top-level central (upid, or self if upid==-1), sorting group members by mvir descending, then forcing the central to the head of the chain before linking: central -> sat1 -> sat2 -> ... -> -1. The explicit central-first step matters for stripped centrals (a central lighter than one of its satellites): SAGE's satellite iterator starts at Halo[central].NextHaloInFOFGroup and would otherwise skip the group. Implemented via utils.fof_topology.build_fof_chains.

SubhaloLen.notes: Consistent Trees does not output particle counts. Estimated as round(mvir / m_particle) where m_particle is the simulation particle mass in Msun/h. m_particle must be supplied via driver config or computed from Omega_M, box size, and N_particles. For BolshoiP (250 Mpc/h, 2048^3 particles, Omega_M=0.307115) m_particle ≈ 1.55e8 Msun/h.

Group_M_Crit200.notes: Column index 40 in the ASCII file. Mass within the radius enclosing 200 times the critical density, as computed by Rockstar.

Group_M_Mean200.notes: Column index 39. Mass within the radius enclosing 200 times the mean (background) density. Optional field; sentinel 0.0 if column is absent.

Group_M_TopHat200.notes: Column index 10. Consistent Trees mvir uses the Bryan & Norman (1998) virial overdensity criterion Delta_vir(z), which is the standard tophat virial mass. This is the closest available field to Group_M_TopHat200. Optional field; sentinel 0.0 acceptable.

SubhaloPos.notes: Columns 17, 18, 19. On-disk values in kpc/h for both output formats: the HDF5 reader multiplies by 0.001 post-read; binary_writer divides by 1000 before packing. Output shape (N, 3).

SubhaloVel.notes: Columns 20, 21, 22. Already in km/s physical. Output shape (N, 3).

SubhaloVelDisp.notes: Column 13. Rockstar vrms is the 3D RMS velocity dispersion (sigma_3D = sqrt(3) * sigma_1D under isotropy). LHaloTree convention is the 1D velocity dispersion (Springel+2005). Correction vrms / sqrt(3) is applied.

SubhaloVMax.notes: Column 16. Rockstar vmax is max(sqrt(GM(<r>)/r)) — matches the SAGE definition exactly.

SubhaloSpin.conversion_expr: stack([Jx, Jy, Jz], axis=1) / mvir[:, None] * 1000
SubhaloSpin.notes: Columns 23, 24, 25. Jx/Jy/Jz are total angular momentum vectors (not specific). Dividing by mvir (Msun/h) yields specific angular momentum in (Mpc/h)(km/s); multiplying by 1000 converts to (kpc/h)(km/s) for on-disk storage. On-disk values in (kpc/h)(km/s) for both output formats: the HDF5 reader multiplies by 0.001 post-read; binary_writer divides by 1000 before packing. The dimensionless Spin column (26) is the Peebles spin parameter and cannot be used here. Output shape (N, 3).

SubhaloIDMostBound.notes: Not available in Consistent Trees output. Using sentinel value -1 (int64).

SnapNum.notes: Column 31. Rockstar/Consistent Trees Snap_num is zero-based and matches the SAGE convention directly.

FileNr.notes: Not available in a stable per-halo form. Using sentinel value -1.

pointer_logic.description: Consistent Trees encodes links via global 64-bit halo IDs (id, desc_id, upid) and pre-computed depth-first index fields (Depth_first_ID, Next_coprogenitor_depthfirst_ID). Within each '#tree <root_id>' block halos are nominally stored in depth-first order, but file order is not guaranteed to be strict DFI order in all cases. The combined forest array must therefore be sorted by DFI unconditionally — including single-tree forests — before pointer reconstruction. The driver operates in two modes depending on whether forests.list and locations.dat are present in the input directory. In FOREST MODE (ancillary files present), all available trees belonging to the same Consistent Trees forest are concatenated, DFI-sorted, and passed to pointer reconstruction as one array; this resolves upid references that cross #tree block boundaries, which are common when satellite halos at a given snapshot belong to a host whose descendant tree is separate. Forests are visited in forests.list first-appearance order. In TREE MODE (ancillary files absent, e.g. single-shard Bolshoi runs), each #tree block is processed independently (original behaviour).
pointer_logic.Descendant: Build a dict mapping global id → combined-array index covering all halos in the current output unit (forest or single tree). For each halo, look up desc_id in this dict. If desc_id == -1 or not found, set Descendant = -1. Descendants are always within the same #tree block, so cross-unit lookups are never needed.
pointer_logic.FirstProgenitor: The combined forest array (or single-tree block) is sorted by DFI before reconstruction, ensuring strict depth-first order throughout. The first (most massive) progenitor of halo at index i is at index i+1 provided i+1 < n and halos[i+1].desc_id == halos[i].id. Otherwise FirstProgenitor[i] = -1. The DFI sort is applied unconditionally — even for single-tree forests — because file order is not guaranteed to be strict DFI order, and the i+1 rule is only valid under strict DFI ordering.
pointer_logic.NextProgenitor: Next_coprogenitor_depthfirst_ID is the globally-unique DFI of the next sibling progenitor within the forest. DFIs are globally unique within a forest but are NOT contiguous across #tree blocks, so the subtraction shortcut 'local = Next_coprogenitor_depthfirst_ID - tree_base_dfi' is incorrect and must not be used. Build an explicit dfi→index dict covering all halos in the combined forest array (sorted by DFI) and look up each halo's Next_coprogenitor_depthfirst_ID. If -1 or not found, set NextProgenitor = -1.
pointer_logic.FirstHaloInFOFGroup: upid is the global halo ID of the ultimate host central at the same snapshot. Build an id→index dict covering all halos in the combined output unit (forest in forest mode, single tree in tree mode). For each halo: if upid == -1 set FirstHaloInFOFGroup = self-index; else look up upid in the dict using iterative path-compression (handles sub-sub-halos). If upid is not found (genuine cross-forest or cross-file reference), treat the halo as its own central. In forest mode, the combined array covers the full forest, so nearly all cross-tree upid references within the same forest resolve correctly.
pointer_logic.NextHaloInFOFGroup: Group all halos in the combined array by (snap_num, FirstHaloInFOFGroup_index). Within each group sort by mvir descending and build a singly-linked list: most-massive → next → ... → -1. The central (highest mvir in the group) has NextHaloInFOFGroup pointing to the first satellite; the last satellite has NextHaloInFOFGroup = -1.

simulation_params.particle_mass_note: The driver computes particle mass from the file header (Omega_M, box_size) assuming n_side=2048 (BolshoiP default). For simulations with different N_particles, supply the correct value via --sim-config (key: n_particles_per_side or particle_mass_msun_per_h) at conversion time; otherwise SubhaloLen will be incorrect. Example: BolshoiP (2048^3, 250 Mpc/h, Omega_M=0.307115, h=0.68): m_particle ≈ 1.55e8 Msun/h. Example: Shin-Uchuu (6400^3, 140 Mpc/h, Omega_M=0.30890, h=0.67740): m_particle = 8.97e5 Msun/h (user-confirmed); n_snapshots=70 (snap_idx 0–69, verified 2026-05-07). Formula: Omega_M * 2.775e11 * (box_size)^3 / n_particles^3 [Msun/h]. Example: micro-uchuu (640^3, 100 Mpc/h, Omega_M=0.30890, h=0.67740, n_snapshots=50): m_particle ≈ 3.27e8 Msun/h (user-confirmed 2026-05-14).

known_caveats: SubhaloLen is not provided by Consistent Trees. It is estimated as round(mvir / m_particle) where m_particle is the simulation dark matter particle mass in Msun/h. This is an approximation: it ignores unbound particles and substructure. The true particle count may differ by a few percent.
SubhaloIDMostBound is not available in Consistent Trees output. The sentinel value -1 is written to every halo.

SubhaloSpin uses the total angular momentum vectors Jx, Jy, Jz divided by Mvir to produce specific angular momentum. The Consistent Trees Spin column (Peebles dimensionless spin parameter lambda) is NOT used.

Group_M_TopHat200 is mapped from Mvir, which uses the Bryan & Norman (1998) redshift-dependent virial overdensity Delta_vir(z). This is not identical to a fixed tophat overdensity criterion but is the standard virial mass and the closest available field.

Phantom halos (phantom != 0) are halos interpolated across timesteps by Consistent Trees. These are written to the output as regular halos. Users may wish to filter them if SAGE exhibits unexpected behaviour.

forests.list and locations.dat trigger forest-level processing. When both files are present, all available tree blocks for each forest are concatenated into one array, sorted by DFI unconditionally, and passed to pointer reconstruction as a unit. DFI sorting is applied even to single-tree forests because file order is not guaranteed to be strict DFI order, and the FirstProgenitor i+1 rule requires strict DFI ordering. Forests are visited in forests.list first-appearance order, ensuring Stage 2 test clips are consistent with reference implementations. This resolves cross-tree upid references (cross-tree satellite/host pairs) that would otherwise appear as isolated centrals, leading to too few massive galaxies after SAGE. When only a single shard of a multi-shard simulation is provided (e.g. a Bolshoi tree_1_0_3.dat without other shards), most forests will be incomplete (fewer available trees than listed in forests.list); the driver still concatenates and DFI-sorts whatever blocks are available before reconstruction.

The number of snapshots (n_snapshots) must be confirmed from the simulation metadata. For BolshoiP it is expected to be 180 (snap_num range 0-179), but the actual maximum snap_num in the data should be verified before writing the Header.

Some Consistent Trees outputs include extra trailing columns beyond the standard 59 (e.g. Shin-Uchuu adds Halfmass_Radius at col 59 and rvmax at col 60, giving 61 columns total). The driver accepts any file with >= 59 columns (_NCOLS_MIN check); extra trailing columns are silently ignored.

SAGE requires a non-empty FileWithSnapList parameter; an empty value causes an immediate fatal error. If no pre-existing snap list file is available, extract it from the input data by scanning for unique (snap_idx, scale_factor) pairs (col 31, col 0) and writing one scale factor per line ordered by snap_idx ascending.

Flyby handling is OPT-IN via sim_params['merge_flybys'] (default off). A Consistent-Trees forest routinely contains many independent z=0 FOF centrals (hundreds to thousands in large forests). SAGE's native Consistent-Trees reader applies fix_flybys, which demotes every non-dominant z=0 central to a satellite of the most massive one (and sign-flips its MostBoundID as a marker). Enabling merge_flybys reproduces that behaviour so SAGE-on-converted-output matches SAGE-reading-CTrees-directly. Default OFF leaves flyby groups as independent Type-0 centrals (the L-Halo-native interpretation, matching MIMIC). This is a modelling choice, not a bug fix: enabling it materially changes the z=0 galaxy population.
